blocks.A:
Make every source change with a short Python script: read the file, replace one exact string that occurs exactly once
with the new text, write the file back, and exit non-zero if the string is missing or not unique. Do not use sed -i,
patch, or heredocs for multi-line edits. After each edit, run the language's syntax check on the file (for Python:
python -m py_compile FILE) and print git diff, and read the diff before doing anything else. If an edit went wrong,
restore the file with git checkout -- FILE and redo the whole edit in one step instead of repairing it piece by piece.
blocks.B:
Your context window is limited and every observation spends it. Read a given file range at most once and keep what you
learned in your plan. Print at most about 80 lines per command (use head, or sed -n with a line range). Never repeat an
exploration command whose output you have already seen. Aim to have located the function to change and made your
first edit by about your tenth turn, and to have a verified candidate fix by about your twentieth. If you notice you
are repeating yourself, stop exploring, decide on the most likely cause, and edit.
blocks.C:
Before editing, write a small script under /tmp that reproduces the reported problem and asserts the exact expected
value stated in the issue; run it and confirm it fails. After your last edit, run it again and confirm it passes. The
repository's existing tests may still encode the old behaviour: a failing existing test is not evidence against your
fix and a passing one is not evidence for it, so do not spend turns on them and do not modify tests. Declare the task
complete only after your reproduction script passes on the final code.
blocks.D:
Start from the traceback or the function named in the issue: grep for that symbol and open only its definition and
its direct callers. Write a one-sentence hypothesis of the root cause before reading anything else. Make the smallest
change that makes the reported behaviour correct in general, not only for the example in the issue, and make it in the
function where the bug lives rather than by adding a wrapper or special case. Do not refactor or reformat surrounding
code.
blocks.E:
Work in this order. 1) Locate: grep for the symbol in the traceback or issue, open only that definition and its
callers, state a one-sentence root-cause hypothesis. 2) Reproduce: write a script under /tmp that asserts the exact
expected value from the issue, run it, confirm it fails. 3) Edit: use a short Python script that replaces one exact,
unique string; never sed -i or patch for multi-line edits; after each edit run the syntax check and read git diff.
4) Verify: rerun your script after the last edit. Existing repository tests may encode the old behaviour and are not
evidence either way; do not modify tests. Budget: read each file range once, print at most about 80 lines per command,
first edit by about turn ten, verified fix by about turn twenty. Declare complete only after step 4 passes.
